text:
Dylan Holloway has gone eight games without a goal, and that's the story of his season so far: 3 goals on 5.4 expected, shooting 6.7% when his range sits near 12%. Last season he was a 20th-ranked forward by Evolving-Hockey's wins above replacement, with 13 goals of even-strength offense. The chances haven't left. He's averaging nearly 2.5 shots a game.

The assists have kept him useful (13 points in 18 games), and St. Louis gets 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, six points better than without. That's a winger doing his job everywhere but the finish.

There's a line story too. The Hockey News and Yahoo argued for reuniting him with Robert Thomas and Jimmy Snuggerud, a group that has played together before. Evolving-Hockey's note is that last year's results ran a bit ahead of his chances, so he shouldn't be expected to repeat 2025-26 exactly. He's near the bottom of the league in wins added by goals this season, which is the dry spell in a single number. Watch the shooting percentage: it rarely stays this low on this many looks.
headline: Holloway is due, and the line question matters
